split.rule: Each planted pattern and each recall campaign belongs entirely to dev or entirely to test. No pattern or campaign appears in both sets.

verdict_schema.cause_type: plant | supplier | line | volume | recall | fleet_wide | none
verdict_schema.cause_type_rule: The verdict answers the question as asked. A 'why' question gets the root cause (the supplier behind the spike); a 'which plant/line/supplier' question gets the location the question asks about (the plant, even when the deeper cause is a supplier). fleet_wide is a real rise that is not concentrated in any plant, line, or supplier (P3: the airbag rise is uniform across plants) — it is not 'none'. none means no pattern at all (the negative controls). P3 and the negative controls are therefore graded differently now: P3 expects fleet_wide, a negative control expects none.
verdict_schema.entity: a plant id (e.g. riverside), a supplier id (e.g. acme-brakes), a line id (e.g. riverside-2), a make/model for volume (e.g. honda-pilot), a recall campaign number (e.g. 26V104000), or null for none
verdict_schema.grading: exact match on (cause_type, entity), except where expected carries accepted_entities: then naming any campaign in the set is correct. supporting_queries is checked separately: every id must be a real evidence index and at least one must be present. Grading uses no LLM judging.
verdict_schema.supporting_queries: indices of the evidence blocks the verdict rests on (0-based)
